# LOG reverse engineering bible

The single index of everything known about the ROMs. Every fact is one line with search tags. Detail and evidence live in the linked source document.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Rule:** every session that learns a fact adds one line here in the same session, with its label and its source. A fact that is not in this file is treated as unknown.

---

## 1. How to search

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **If it is not in this bible, read the DISASSEMBLY. Do not reverse engineer it again.**
>
> `C:\Users\josephgonzalez\Documents\GitHub\legacyofgoku2-disasm` is a byte exact disassembly of this
> exact ROM, and `legacyofgoku2-gnu\build\code` already holds 1333 generated `.s` files, so any handler
> can be READ with no build at all.
>
> | Looking for | Open |
> |---|---|
> | What a RAM word is | `legacyofgoku2-disasm\docs\RAM_LEDGER.csv`, 13 words, each with the behaviour test that proves it |
> | Which file holds a function | `legacyofgoku2-disasm\docs\CODE_INDEX.md`, all 1249 starts |
> | The code itself | `legacyofgoku2-gnu\build\code\`: a named function under its own name, an unnamed one as `code_<lowercase address>.s` |
> | Where a function begins and ends | `legacyofgoku2-disasm\tools\code\FUNCTION_BOUNDS.csv` |
>
> Only 204 of the 1249 functions carry a name, so this is not a book of answers. It is the source of
> truth, and it still has to be read. Read the handler BEFORE you interpret a RAM word, an op or a
> symptom. On 2026-11-05 I spent an evening on the ending fight with three RAM labels that were wrong,
> two of them taken from a Grok review and an agent report, and `Sprite_Select` corrected all three in
> about two minutes once the file was open. Buu's Fury has its own pair, `buusfury-disasm` and
> `buusfury-decomp`.

Use these tag shapes. Each one is unique, so a plain text search finds every line about it.

| Search for | Finds | Id |
|---|---|---|
| `@0x0801F394` | A GBA address (code, ROM data as `@0x08xxxxxx`, RAM as `@0x02xxxxxx` or `@0x03xxxxxx`) |
| `rom:0x3B4E90` | A file offset in the ROM (address minus `0x08000000`) |
| `flag:195` | A story flag |
| `set:56` | A sprite set id |
| `pal:88` | A shared OBJ palette index |
| `char:gohan` | A character (`gohan`, `piccolo`, `vegeta`, `trunks`, `goku`, `hercule`) |
| `#codec` `#sprite` `#save` `#form` `#story` `#map` `#palette` `#hud` `#status` `#portrait` `#text` `#script` `#antipiracy` `#debug` `#tool` `#decision` `#open` `#boot` `#object` `#state` `#combat` `#item` `#menu` `#input` `#sound` | A topic |
| `game:bf` `game:log2eu` | A fact about Buu's Fury or the Europe LoG II. No game tag means LoG II USA |
| **A screenshot is matched to a ROM map by PIXELS, and the 5 bit to 8 bit colour conversion must be `(i << 3) \| (i >> 2)`, not `i << 3`.** With `i << 3` the owner's 2026-11-07 reference screenshot matched 0 of 378 blocks against all 327 maps; with the replicate-high-bits conversion it matched 320. Also measure the scale and the PHASE: that shot is 5x with one column of the first native pixel cropped away, so a plain `resize` samples the wrong pixel | #tool #palette | C (both conversions run over all 327 maps; `match_shot_all.txt`) | SCN | B2057 |
| **Tile-set membership does not locate a screenshot, because the 168 chunk frames are a global pool.** 320 of the owner's 378 reference blocks are tiles some zone 2 map loads and 17 different maps hold 8 of them, yet the best POSITIONAL placement over every zone 2, 8 and 10 VARIATION found 145 of 378, on map 2,6 variation 2, ahead of 124 on 2,32 var 1 and 118 on 8,41. Rank by RARE blocks instead: exactly one block is held by one map only (2,6). The shot's dominant colour (156,156,0) is palette index 35, the OLIVE grass, so it is East District variation 2, not variation 1. LIKELY cause of the residual miss: the grass is an animated tile group and the shot catches a frame the reader does not load | #tool #map | C (counts), L (the animation cause) | SCN | B2058 |

Labels: **C** = CONFIRMED (proved, evidence in the source doc), **L** = LIKELY, **S** = SPECULATIVE, **O** = my own statement (from memory or play, not checked in the ROM).

Upstream `jeremycollake/jcalg1` `jccomp.inc`: `INITIAL_BASE equ 8`, `DecrementIndex1 = 027fh`, `DecrementIndex2 = 037ffh`, `DecrementIndex3 = 010000h`, `SHORT_RANGE = 1111111b`, `SHORT_BITS = 7`, `ONEBYTE_PHRASE_BITS = 4`, `LITERAL_BITSIZE = 1`, `BLOCK_SIZE equ 256`: each equals the LoG II ARM routine (offset width 8, length bonus thresholds, 7-bit short match, 4-bit one-byte phrase, 7 + 1-bit literal width, 256-byte raw block). JCALG1's own header is `{u16 'JC', u32 size, u32 checksum}`; LoG II uses `{u32 type, u32 size}` instead. | Script VM compare and branch ops: op 15 (`lt`, `@0x080090CA`) pops b, then replaces a with `a < b` (`cmp r3,r2 ; blt`), so `push a ; push b ; lt` = a < b. | BF glyph draw `0x0803F70C`: fill colour (text context +3 = 2) where the column bit is set, else outline colour (+2 = 1) where a 4-neighbour bit is set (left, right, up, down; no diagonals). Column c lands at pen + c; outline columns at pen - 1 and pen + width; 17 rows. `0x0802BECC`: buffer W = (width + 33) & ~31 by 32 rows, pen x = W/2 - (width + 1) / 2 (mode 1, centred), pen y = 10, OBJ at (x - W/2, y - 16). So bit b of column c is on screen at (x - (width + 1) // 2 + c, y - 6 + b) | game:bf #text #font | C (listing), C (screenshot: 8 of 11424 text-band pixels off) | CH3 | B0802 |

| Script base ops 17-20, 27 and 28, from their handlers. Table word 17 is 0, so the interpreter ends a record itself. Op 20 (`@0x08009129`) pops one value and discards it. Op 27 (`@0x08009251`) pops a count into the loop area at +0x44, and op 28 (`@0x0800926D`) counts it down and jumps back while it is non-zero. | The compact push op `1d` takes a count byte and then one zigzag varint a value (`scene_lib.zigzag`, moved there from `piccolo_gi_scene`): u = v * 2 for v >= 0 and (-v) * 2 + 1 for v < 0, then 7 bits a byte, most significant group first, every group but the last carrying 0x80. So 8 gives `10`, 24 gives `30`, 84 gives `81 28`, 128 gives `82 00` and 272 gives `84 20`. Bit 0 of the first group is the sign, which is how the card 4 exit records push `OFF_Y` = -40. The one-value form is `00 nn`, used when a single value is 0 to 255, and it writes the raw byte | #script | C (`scripts\permanent\scene\scene_lib.py` `zigzag` and `push`, plus every push in `chapter_cards` record 0 decoded by hand) | C4M | B0946 |

| The face-the-player step tick `@0x08010038` decides as follows (bytes `ac4207db002a02dd03220a7409e002220a7406e0002b02dd00220a7401e001220a74` at rom:0x1006A). It reads the player `[0x03001FA8]`, takes dx and dy as player +0x158/+0x15C minus NPC +0x158/+0x15C, then `cmp r4,r5 ; blt`, where r4 is \|dx\| and r5 is \|dy\|. When \|dx\| >= \|dy\| it goes horizontal: facing 3 when dx > 0, else 2. When \|dx\| < \|dy\| it goes vertical: facing 0 when dy > 0, else 1. So an exact diagonal falls to the horizontal branch. It stores the result at NPC +0x10 every frame it runs | #script #object #sprite | C (hand decode of the 34 bytes, pinned by `test_every_scripted_facing_is_the_one_the_step_picks`) | CJA | B0951 |

| The scene VM has TWO dispatch tables and both have a hard end. Base table `rom:0x3B5C00` holds exactly **17** entries (base ops 0-16, the pushes, `set_var` and the 13 arithmetic and compare ops); word 17 is `0x00000000`. Ext table `rom:0x3B5D28` holds exactly **145** entries (ext 0-144); word 145 is `0x03000E90`, which is IWRAM, not a handler. The two tables are `0x128` apart, which is 74 words, so they are NOT adjacent and the gap is not table data. Base ops 17-29 (`end`, `jmp`, `jz`, `drop`, `loop_begin`, `loop_end`, `push_list`) are therefore NOT dispatched through the table: the interpreter handles them inline. Consequence: our `scene_lib.EXT_OPS` entry **145 `card` is past the end of the ext table** and cannot be an ext op | #script #story | C (both tables walked to the first non-pointer word, `scripts\permanent\disasm\ext_ops.py`) | OPS | B1021 |
| Scene VM calling convention, read from the handlers: `r0` enters an ext handler holding the operand stack `{u32 depth at [r0+0], values at [r0+4+4*i] for i in 0..depth-1}`, so the TOP value is at `[r0 + 4*depth]`. Handlers take four shapes, and a tool that knows only the first mis-reads the other three. **1 CONSUMER:** pops each argument with `SUB rX,#0x1` then `STR rX,[stack,#0x0]`; the SUB and the STR are NOT adjacent, an `LSL` for the slot address sits between them. **2 PREDICATE:** computes `ADD rN,depth*4,r0`, loads `[rN+0]` and stores its RESULT back to `[rN+0]`, leaving depth alone, which is what base op 19 `jz` requires. **3 ALIASED:** copies the stack pointer out of `r0` first (`ADD r1,r0,#0x0`) and pops through that register. **4 NON-VM:** discards the stack and loads a global into `r0` before its call | #script | C (ext 31 consumer, ext 19 predicate, ext 49 aliased, ext 63 non-VM, all four handlers read) | OPS | B1022 |

Counting pops across a whole handler body scored ext 55 `face` as 3 arguments when it takes 2, and inflated every one of the 12 actor ops by exactly one. Any future arity work must stop counting at the first call | #script #tool | C (ext 55 `code_08009efc.s`: two pops, then `BL Sprite_Select`, then `BL Heap_Alloc`, then `STR r1,[r0,#0x4]` and `STR r1,[r0,#0x0]` into the 12-byte command) | OPS | B1023 |

| **A scene table's length rule, settled.** `scene_lib.table_length()` walks while a word is an END entry or a record pointer, and stops at the first word that is neither. | **The "visited" bit is NOT indexed by the map table index, so appending a map entry cannot reach the save.** `sub_080041A6` tests and `sub_080040EE` sets, and both walk the SAME structure: a pc-literal holds `+0x00` a group count and `+0x04` a group list; each group has `+0x14` an entry count and `+0x18` the entries; each entry has byte `+0x00` zone, byte `+0x01` area and a `u16` bit index at `+0x02`. The bit is `save + 0xE0 + 7 + (n >> 3)`, bit `n & 7`, where n is that entry's own u16. A (zone, area) pair that matches no entry falls out of both loops: the test returns 0 at `loc_08004206` and the setter returns at `loc_08004138` **without writing a byte**. But growing list A by one item moves list B from `+0x2B0` to `+0x2B8`, moves the sub-object after it from `+0x40C` to `+0x41C`, and takes the allocation to `0x454`. `+0x2B0` is built at `rom:0x4A52`, `rom:0x4AF2` and `rom:0x4CA2` as `mov rX,#0x2b ; lsl rX,rX,#4`, and `0x2B8` is not 16 times any 8 bit immediate, so each of those three sites needs an extra instruction it has no room for. `+0x40C` is built at `rom:0x4A5C` as `add r0,#0xff ; add r0,#0x5d` off the same register. The three `0x2b` immediates are NOT the quest count: `0x2B0` does not fit a Thumb 8 bit immediate and the compiler builds it the same way it builds `0x11C` from `add #0xff ; add #0x1d` two instructions earlier. The coincidence that `0x2B0` equals `43 * 16` is what makes this trap look like a count bump | #script #menu #decision | C (all five sites disassembled and the two gaps computed) | BTM | | B2339 |

Entry 0's pointer, the word at `rom:0x6D68E8`, is `0x086D6B8C`, which equals `table + 688` only because the text pool was laid immediately after the table. So a copy of the 688 byte table in expansion keeps all 43 texts working where they are | #script #menu | C (the entry read and the pointer resolved) | BTM | | B2340 |

| **`sub_080086D4` is the PLAYER SPRITE CONSTRUCTOR and the only thing that gives the player a body.** It allocates 0x1A0 bytes through `@0x0801F08C`, writes its vtable, registers itself with `STR r4, [0x03001FA8]` (`Sprite_CurrentDirectory`), then reads the PARTY ROSTER to pick the character and loads its graphics through `@0x08021D2C`. **It is reachable only from the three map ops**, `ext 35`, `ext 38` and `ext 39`, through `@0x0800C584` and `@0x0800C664`. **(CORRECTED by AR6, and the error cost a build: `ext 35` does NOT reach it.** Only `@0x0800C584` calls the constructor, and its only callers are `sub_080099D2` (ext 38) and `sub_08009A88` (ext 39). `ext 35` and `ext 36` reach `@0x0800C664` only, which never builds a player. | `test_future_androids.run_branch(rom, record, player_spot)` RUNS a death record's VM ops in 32 bits with `ext 143` answering a given spot, and returns which arm ran, the point `ext 144` unpacks, the point `ext 62` places him at (or None when no reposition ran), and the stack depth at the end op. `scene_harness` cannot do this job: its ext handling clears the whole stack, so a record that reads a value back with `ext 0` to `ext 3` loses it. A plain ext op pops its DOCUMENTED ARITY there, never \"clear the stack\", because clearing would hide exactly the leftover value that op 17 turns into a table index | #tool #script | C (every open cell of map 1,100, all four arms) | RG4 | | B2160 |
| A branch test that only pins bytes needs a NEGATIVE CONTROL, and one fits in the same test file: rewrite a constant IN THE BUILT BYTES with an encoding of the same length and assert the arm flips. Moving the bottom edge of the view from 487 to 8000 (both two zigzag varint bytes, so no later op moves) stops the talk spot teleporting while it still walks him, which proves that bound is read | #tool #script | C | RG4 | | B2161 |
| Trap: `scene_lib.listing()` folds every pushed value into the NEXT ext op and names it from that op's own argument list, so `ext 56 (0, 11)` prints as `face_alt(set=0, dir=11)` and a push meant for `ext 144` prints as an argument of `ext 0`. Read the raw ops, not the listing, whenever a record pushes a value that an op two or three ops later consumes | #tool #script | C (v6 read-back against the raw bytes) | RG4 | | B2162 |
| `scripts\one-time\2026-11-07-rung4-deaths\street_census.py <rom> [zone area]` enumerates every keep-out carrier a map entry and its layout can name: layout props, the entry's break records, its items (through `scene_probe.item`, which dispatches the spot on the factory, `+0x08` for an NPC and `+0x0C` for an enemy), its regions, the layout door list, pickups, markers and the collision frame. It prints 'the search returned nothing' for an empty carrier rather than claiming none exists | #tool #map | C | RG4 | | B2163 |
| **A census of a rule must RUN THE SHIPPED BYTECODE, not a Python restatement of it.** `landing_census.py` imports `run_branch` from the test module, drives a built ROM's own death record with `ext 143` answering each open cell, and scores the stop, the visible part of the walk, the walk length and the fraction of it inside the view. An offset constant could be imported; a clamp cannot, and a second implementation of one would drift | #tool #script | C (v7 and v8 scored under one measure) | RG4 | | B2164 |
| **A BizHawk `.State` loads only on the ROM that made it**, so a trial build needs its own cold-boot run before any resume. `make_v8_jobs.py land` boots a plateau trial ROM, plays the farewell and the credits with the A macro and saves a state at the android street in 26,822 frames; every later job resumes it in about 2,500. The arrival scene eats direction presses for about 700 frames, so a job that wants the player to MOVE must tap A for roughly 48 cycles first | #tool #emu | C (six runs) | RG4 | | B2165 |
| Every bible data row carries a stable id in its last cell, `B0001` form, assigned once by `assign_ids` in `scripts\permanent\disasm\symbols.py` and never renumbered. Cite the id, never a line number: a merge moves every line below its insert point, and on 2026-11-07, 5 of the 13 in-bible "row N" citations already named a different fact. `whatis B0001` finds the row, matched whole against the Id cell, because 13 of the 2030 ids also appear inside another row's hex byte string. | #tool | C | BID | B2183 |
| Id gap: `assign_ids` takes the next id from the highest id in the file, so deleting the newest row frees its id for reuse. `test_bible_ids.test_an_id_is_never_reused_after_its_row_is_deleted` is an expected failure that keeps this visible. A fix needs a high-water mark stored outside the rows. | #tool #open | C | BID | B2184 |
| The bible table shape is `Fact, Tags, Label, Src, Id`. A parser reads the Id cell off the end FIRST, then reads the rest, because 146 decision and question rows hold only 3 cells and would otherwise read their id as Src, and 9 fact rows split into 5, 8 or 16 cells on an escaped pipe inside the fact text. | #tool | C | BID | B2185 |
| **A save state answers "where is this actor's box" faster than any ROM walk, because the live actor names its own set.** `state_dump.py` prints each actor as `object`, which is already the anchor minus `0x158`, so a second subtraction reads garbage. From that base, `[+0x10]` is the direction block index, `[+0x48]` is the set POINTER, and `set + 0xC + 16 * index` is the box `Rect_FromDefinition` builds from. On `finale_poses_wip1.ss3` the anchors are the player at (424,608), Trunks at (424,480), Cell at (424,416) and one more at (256,1) whose owner was not identified | #tool #sprite | C (used to settle the beam start, 2026-11-09) | BSP | | B2325 |
| **A row map of one sprite frame cannot find an arm. A pixel DIFF against the other frame of the same row can.** Both of the finale's Trunks frames carry the same Super Saiyan hair over rows 1-15, so a "which rows carry pixels" listing of the firing frame reads as one solid block and puts the hands in the wrong place. Rendering both frames and colouring only the pixels one has and the other lacks shows the raised arms at once | #tool #sprite | C (2026-11-09; the first reading put the hands 8 px wrong) | BSP | | B2326 |
| `scripts\permanent\art\portrait_blanks.py` exports the portrait frames and backdrops as 64x64 PNGs to `art\portrait-kit`: `frames\` the ring with a transparent middle, `backdrops\` the rebuilt spotlight, `blanks\` the two composited and ready to draw on, `proof\` each rebuild beside the real portraits it came from, and a README naming which id uses which. It takes `--rom` so it reads a build. **It deletes its own output from the previous run** by four exact name patterns, because an earlier run of it wrote 6 frames and 18 backdrops and after the method was corrected those became 2 and 6, leaving stale files that looked current | #tool #sprite #portrait | C | PBK | | B2358 |

| A per-actor palette may be reachable WITHOUT touching the shared OBJ palette: colour depth is per sprite (OAM `attr0` bit 13) and the palette bank is `attr2` bits 12-15, so a 4bpp OBJ would get its own 16-colour bank. The precondition is already confirmed on our ROM: `@0x08007784` copies the frame record's `+4` word (attr0, attr1) into OAM verbatim (bible row 119), so an actor's own record decides bit 13. Their mechanism addresses (`0x0800F254`, `0x0800F2A0`) are BUU's, not ours, so both sites must be re-derived around `@0x08007784`.
